producer_version: 3.5.1 and 4.2.0 (the official demo/sample catalog these two Ant Movie Catalog releases ship with, exported/saved unmodified from each)
creation_steps: These are Ant Movie Catalog's own bundled sample catalog -- the demonstration data that ships inside the official 3.5.1 and 4.2.0 installers -- contributed to this repository by its owner from their own licensed installs, unmodified from what the installer provides. Both files hold the same seven-movie demo set (The Matrix, Lethal Weapon 4, Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade, Memento, Jurassic Park, and two more), each with an embedded JPEG or PNG poster; the 4.2.0 file additionally defines eight custom fields (one of every type except ftReal1 and ftVirtual) with sample values, and both include native-format supplementary ('extra') records.
provenance: Contributed directly to this repository by its owner from their own locally installed, licensed copies of Ant Movie Catalog 3.5.1 and 4.2.0, specifically to give this port genuine populated-catalog native-format evidence (custom fields, embedded pictures, supplementary records) for the first time -- see docs/decisions.md ADR-0001 and docs/PORT_AUDIT.md's P0 evidence gate. This is the application's own bundled sample data, not the contributor's personal catalog. Not independently authenticated beyond the file contents and the owner's own account of their origin.
expected_contents: Ant Movie Catalog's own bundled seven-movie demo catalog, saved unmodified from genuine 3.5.1 and 4.2.0 installs. Both hold identical movie data (title, year, length, rating, and an embedded JPEG/PNG poster per movie -- promotional artwork bundled with the application itself, not user-contributed personal data). The 4.2.0 file additionally carries eight custom-field definitions spanning boolean, date, integer, list (with real list values), currency/real, string, text, and URL types, and native supplementary ('extra') records. Found and fixed a real, total-parse-failure bug in this port (docs/PORT_AUDIT.md finding 39): a List-type custom field crashed the native reader outright, because the reader compared the field-type string against the bare literal 'list' instead of upstream's actual serialized identifier 'ftList' (confirmed in the checked-in Delphi source's own `ConvertFieldTypeToString`); the writer had the mirror-image bug, silently dropping list values instead of writing them.
